profiles.meeting_scenario: An internal coordination meeting at a research software startup preparing a beta demo and paper artifact for Snakemaker. Priya, who owns the terminal instrumentation and workflow export layer, and Lucas, who owns notebook conversion and the chat assistant, need to align on the handoff between the recorder output and the AI generation stack. The agenda is to confirm what the "v2 schema" handoff includes, what "session replay" will provide to downstream components, whether environment tracking is sufficient for the notebook-to-workflow path, and what counts as being "demo-ready" for Friday's integrated branch. The expected outcome is an apparently clear plan for Priya to deliver the recorder/export artifacts and for Lucas to integrate them into the beta demo branch.

members.name: Priya Nair
members.expertise: workflow infrastructure, provenance capture, Snakemake integration
members.background: Priya previously built internal reproducibility tooling for genomics pipelines and now leads the terminal tracking and workflow export components of Snakemaker.
members.private_state: She wants to freeze the recorder-side contract this week, avoid expanding the payload size before the demo, and keep responsibility for environment reconstruction out of her team's scope.
hidden_assumptions: "Session replay" means a normalized execution summary derived from terminal activity, not a raw chronological shell transcript.
"Schema v2" refers to the protobuf event contract emitted by the recorder service because that is the interface her team version-controls.
"Environment tracking" for the beta means per-rule Conda YAMLs plus command-observed tool versions, not full reconstruction of system packages or transient notebook installs.
"Demo-ready" means the integrated flow works reliably on the curated RNA-seq showcase example without crashes or manual code edits.

members.name: Lucas Meyer
members.expertise: LLM-assisted code transformation, notebook analysis, developer-facing copilots
members.background: Lucas came from a computational biology tooling lab and now leads Snakemaker's notebook-to-workflow conversion and chat assistant experience.
members.private_state: He wants the demo to show breadth across multiple examples, needs richer provenance context for the assistant's explanations, and hopes to avoid manual patching during the Friday run-through.
hidden_assumptions: "Session replay" includes the ordered command history, working-directory changes, environment mutations, and install steps in a form the assistant can narrate back to the user.
"Schema v2" refers to the canonical JSON intermediate representation consumed by the generator and assistant layers because that is the format he integrates against.
"Environment tracking" should let the generated workflow explain and recreate notebook-time package installs, including pip and non-Conda dependencies that affected execution.
"Demo-ready" means the notebook conversion path works across the three planned showcase examples with only natural-language steering, not hand-authored fixes.

misalignment_points.surface_form: Both talk about wiring up "session replay" for the generator and assistant.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya means a compact, normalized provenance summary: commands collapsed into rule-relevant file and process transitions with non-essential shell details stripped out.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas means a faithful ordered replay of the user's terminal session, including shell context and install history, so the assistant can explain transformation decisions.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: In coordination meetings, "session replay" sounds like a well-known internal component name, so each assumes the other is using the established meaning from their own subteam.

misalignment_points.topic: Which v2 schema is being frozen
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both refer to "schema v2" as the interface that will be ready for integration.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya is talking about recorder-side protobuf event schema v2 in the instrumentation repository.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas is talking about the downstream JSON intermediate representation v2 used by the rule generator and chat assistant.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Both schemas are genuinely called v2 in adjacent repos, and because they are linked in the pipeline, saying "once v2 lands" feels naturally coherent even though they are naming different artifacts.

misalignment_points.topic: What counts as demo-ready notebook support
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both agree the notebook conversion path should be "demo-ready" by Friday.
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya thinks demo-ready means one polished, curated showcase notebook converts and runs end-to-end without crashing.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas thinks demo-ready means all three planned showcase notebooks convert into modular workflows without manual repair beyond user-facing chat prompts.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: The phrase "demo-ready" usually functions as a shorthand status label, and both are being cooperative about Friday readiness rather than explicitly enumerating acceptance thresholds.

misalignment_points.topic: What is included in environment tracking
misalignment_points.surface_form: Both say the handoff already includes "environment tracking".
misalignment_points.member_a_understanding: Priya includes only the Conda environment files and versions inferable from tracked commands that become attached to generated Snakemake rules.
misalignment_points.member_b_understanding: Lucas includes the broader provenance needed to explain or recreate notebook execution, such as pip installs inside cells, base image assumptions, and ad-hoc package mutations.
misalignment_points.why_undetected: Environment tracking is already advertised as a product capability, so neither expects to restate the exact boundary of what is in or out; each assumes the obvious interpretation is shared.
